topology.why: A topic exchange stores nothing. Until a consumer has started once, its queue does not exist, so every event published in that window is discarded while the publish call still returns success. StoryContentManager therefore declares the consumer queues and bindings as well as its own exchange.
topology.target: Each queue definition stays in its consumer's repository and is applied at deploy time, whether or not that consumer has ever run. Then the consumer owns its queue again without the first-start window reopening.

events.name: scene-content.updated
events.note: Carries the complete scene aggregate, not a notification to go and fetch it (ADR-005).

fields.name: sceneVersion
fields.note: Discard anything not newer than what you hold.

fields.name: choices
fields.note: choiceId, label, beat, destinationSceneId, weight, requirements[], effects[]. An effect is a kind plus its argument: GRANT_ITEM, GRANT_QUEST, COMPLETE_QUEST, MODIFY_STAT or GRANT_FLAG. A requirement is STORY_FLAG or ITEM.

fields.name: grantedItemIds
fields.note: On a choice. Exactly the itemId values of the GRANT_ITEM effects. Kept only for consumers written against 1.0.0; new ones read effects instead. Removing it is a breaking change and will be announced first.

deadLetter.why: A rejected message has to end up somewhere a human can look. Declaring the exchange alone would not have been enough: an exchange with nothing bound to it discards what it receives, so each dead-letter queue is declared and bound by its own name.

openIssues.short: Who assigns the per-character sequence number?
openIssues.detail: If StoryPathManager assigns it on insert, ordering still depends on arrival order and nothing is gained.

openIssues.short: The .proto sits in the caller's tree.
openIssues.detail: It describes StoryPathManager's API but lives in RecapManager's source, inverting the ownership rule.

openIssues.short: No service has been assigned GraphQL.
openIssues.detail: At least one backend service must expose it. SceneManager and CharacterManager are the candidates.
OAuth/OIDC with at least one external provider is required, in addition to our own JWT.

openIssues.short: The serverless component is not built.
openIssues.detail: TextToSpeechManager as a KEDA ScaledJob scaled on queue depth is what satisfies the serverless requirement.
8081 and 8090 are taken, and 8092 is implied by RecapManager's JWT_ISSUER default without being written down.

openIssues.short: No logging or monitoring solution has been chosen.
openIssues.detail: The exam requires one suited to distributed systems. What matters is correlation: an id that survives from an HTTP request through the broker into a consumer is worth more than per-service logs that cannot be joined. Promtail, Loki, Prometheus and Grafana are drawn on the Kubernetes tab as a proposal, not a decision.

openIssues.short: How images reach the local cluster is undecided.
openIssues.detail: kind load versus a local registry. The CI/CD pipeline has to push somewhere, which argues for the registry.
